text:
Blake Coleman is 34, won two Stanley Cups with Tampa Bay, and is 26 games into his first season with the Wild after 392 in Calgary. He's playing the way he always has: 50 hits, penalty killing, and shots from close in. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) puts him at the 87th percentile among forwards for chances from the home plate in front of the net.

He has eight goals on 8.2 expected, so the finishing is honest, and 14 points in 26 games. His point rate sits slightly above his talent range, helped by a team that has points in 15 straight. Heather Rule noted that the Wild lead the NHL in empty-net goals, and Coleman has chipped in. At five on five Minnesota takes 53% of the expected goals with him on. Evolving-Hockey had him 58th among forwards in wins above replacement last season, so he arrived as more than a checker. Our range projects 35 to 53 points and 19 to 31 goals. The goals are the real value.
